title: Mock Test 04 (harder)

questions.question: NavIC, developed by ISRO, is:
options: a launch vehicle for small satellites
questions.explanation: NavIC (IRNSS) gives positioning over India and about 1500 km around it.

questions.question: The Aditya-L1 spacecraft observes the Sun from:
options: a halo orbit around the Sun–Earth Lagrange point L1
questions.explanation: L1 lies about 1.5 million km sunward, giving an uninterrupted view of the Sun.

questions.question: UPI Lite is designed for:
options: small-value payments from an on-device balance without entering the UPI PIN each time
payments by feature phones over a voice call
questions.explanation: UPI Lite is an on-device wallet for small payments; UPI 123PAY is the feature-phone option.

questions.question: The IndiaAI Mission approved by the Union Cabinet in 2024 focuses mainly on:
options: banning AI tools in government offices
a single national chatbot for railway bookings
building AI compute capacity, datasets and Indian foundation models
questions.explanation: The mission funds GPU compute, datasets (AIKosh), foundation models, skilling and start-ups.

questions.question: At the Paris 2024 Olympics, Neeraj Chopra won which medal in the men's javelin?
options: He did not win a medal
questions.explanation: Arshad Nadeem won gold with an Olympic record; Chopra took silver.

questions.question: ISRO's headquarters is located in:
questions.explanation: Sriharikota is the launch centre; VSSC is in Thiruvananthapuram; SAC is in Ahmedabad.

questions.question: The International Telecommunication Union (ITU), the UN agency for ICT standards, is headquartered in:
questions.explanation: ITU is in Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.question: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the World Wide Web in 1989 while working at:
questions.explanation: He proposed it at CERN near Geneva.

questions.question: A is twice as efficient as B. Together they finish a job in 14 days. A alone would take:
questions.explanation: A makes 2 chairs a day and B 1: total 3 × 14 = 42 chairs; A alone 42/2 = 21 days.

questions.question: 12 men working 8 hours a day finish a job in 10 days. How many days will 16 men working 6 hours a day take?
A man goes to a town at 40 km/h and returns at 60 km/h. The whole trip takes 5 hours. How far is the town?
In a 1 km race A beats B by 100 m, and B beats C by 100 m. By how much does A beat C?
questions.explanation: When A runs 1000, B runs 900 and C runs 900 × 0.9 = 810: A wins by 190 m.

questions.question: A town of 50,000 grows 10% in the first year, falls 10% in the second and grows 20% in the third. Its population after three years is:
By selling 33 m of cloth, a shopkeeper gains the selling price of 11 m. His gain percent is:
A dealer claims to sell at cost price but uses a 900 g weight for 1 kg. His gain percent is:
questions.explanation: He gives 900 g for the price of 1000 g: gain 100/900 = 11.11%.

questions.question: A sum doubles in 5 years at simple interest. In how many years will it become four times itself?
questions.explanation: Interest equal to the sum takes 5 years (20% a year); three times the sum takes 15 years.

questions.question: The compound interest on Rs. 8,000 for 1 year at 10% per annum, compounded half-yearly, is:
questions.explanation: 5% per half-year: 8000 × 1.05² = 8820, so CI = 820.

questions.question: Two vessels hold milk and water in the ratios 3 : 1 and 5 : 3. Equal quantities from both are mixed. The ratio of milk to water in the mixture is:
questions.explanation: Milk fraction (3/4 + 5/8)/2 = 11/16, water 5/16.

questions.question: The incomes of A and B are in the ratio 5 : 4 and their expenses in the ratio 3 : 2. Each saves Rs. 3,000. A's income is:
How many times in a day (24 hours) are the hands of a clock at right angles?
questions.explanation: 22 times in 12 hours (twice an hour, minus 2 shared cases), so 44 in a day.

questions.question: Two cards are drawn together from a well-shuffled pack of 52. The probability that both are kings is:
Find the next term: 4, 6, 12, 30, 90, ?

Statements: All servers are machines. Some machines are routers.
Conclusions: I. Some servers are routers. II. No server is a router.
questions.explanation: Neither follows alone, but I and II are exact opposites about servers and routers, so one of them must be true.

questions.question: Six people A to F sit around a round table facing the centre. A sits opposite D. B is second to the right of A. E is immediately to the right of D. C is not next to B. Who sits immediately to the left of A?
questions.explanation: Fix A: D opposite, B two seats to A's right, E next to D on D's right. The two seats left are beside A; C cannot be beside B, so C is on A's left.

questions.question: Introducing a man, a woman said, "His wife is the only daughter of my mother." How is the woman related to the man?
questions.explanation: The only daughter of her mother is the woman herself, so she is his wife.

questions.question: Early in the morning Ravi stands facing a pole. The pole's shadow falls exactly to his right. Which direction is he facing?
questions.explanation: Morning sun is in the east, so shadows fall west. West on his right means he faces south.

questions.question: If CAT is coded as 3120 (each letter replaced by its position, written one after another), then DOG is coded as:
In a row of 40 students, A is 13th from the left and B is 9th from the right. How many students are between them?
questions.explanation: B is 40 − 9 + 1 = 32nd from the left; between = 32 − 13 − 1 = 18.

questions.question: ACE : BDF :: MOQ : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward.

questions.question: Find the next term: 2, 6, 30, 210, ?
questions.explanation: Products of the first primes: 2, 2·3, 2·3·5, 2·3·5·7, then ×11.

questions.question:
What is P's present age?
I. P is 4 years older than Q.
II. The sum of the present ages of P and Q is 40.
questions.explanation: Neither alone fixes P, but together P − Q = 4 and P + Q = 40 give P = 22.

questions.question: Find the odd one out:
questions.explanation: The others skip one letter each time (T V X would fit); TVY skips two at the end.

questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to PRUDENT:
questions.explanation: Prudent = acting with care and thought for the future.

questions.question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to AMBIGUOUS:
questions.explanation: Ambiguous = open to more than one meaning.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Hardly had he reached the lab _____ the power failed.
questions.explanation: The pattern is "hardly ... when" ("no sooner ... than").

questions.question: Identify the part with an error: "One of the servers / have crashed / since / last night."
questions.explanation: The subject is "one", so the verb is singular: "has crashed".

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The new policy will come _____ effect from 1 December.
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is "come into effect".

questions.question: One word for "a formal written request signed by many people and sent to an authority":
questions.explanation: An affidavit is a sworn statement; a circular is a notice sent to many.

questions.question: Choose the passive form of: "Someone has stolen the projector."
options: The projector was stolen by someone.
questions.explanation: Present perfect active → has been + past participle; an indefinite agent is dropped.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word:
questions.explanation: Double c and double m: accommodation.

questions.question: A computer that works on continuously varying physical quantities such as voltage or pressure is called:
questions.explanation: Analog = continuous values; digital = discrete; hybrid = both.

questions.question: In IEEE 754 single precision (32-bit) floating point, how many bits hold the exponent?
questions.explanation: 1 sign bit, 8 exponent bits (bias 127), 23 fraction bits; double uses 11.

questions.question: 0x3F + 0x2C equals:
The Gray code of the binary number 1011 is:
TLB lookup takes 10 ns and a memory access 100 ns, with a TLB hit ratio of 90% and a single-level page table. The effective memory access time is:
40% of a program can run in parallel. By Amdahl's law, the speed-up on 4 processors is about:
What is the output?
questions.explanation: q points to p, which points to x, so **q = 20 changes x.

questions.explanation: *(a + 1) is row 1; adding 2 and dereferencing gives a[1][2] = 6.

questions.question: For the linked list 1 → 2 → 3, what does f(head) print?
questions.explanation: The recursive call comes before printf, so nodes are printed on the way back: in reverse.

questions.question: A binary tree has inorder 10 20 30 40 50 60 and preorder 40 20 10 30 50 60. Its postorder traversal is:
questions.explanation: Root 40; left subtree 20 (10, 30); right subtree 50 with right child 60.

questions.question: The maximum number of comparisons binary search needs on a sorted array of 1000 elements is:
The best-case time complexity of insertion sort (input already sorted) is:
questions.explanation: Each element is compared once with its left neighbour and not moved.

questions.question: Graph edges (taken in alphabetical order): A→B, A→C, B→D, B→E, C→F, E→F. A recursive depth-first search from A visits the vertices in the order:
options: A B C D E F
A C F B E D
A B D E F C
A B E F D C
questions.explanation: A, then B and its subtree D, E, F; C's only neighbour F is already visited.

questions.question: Keys 10, 20 and 30 are inserted in that order into an empty AVL tree. Which rebalancing happens?
questions.explanation: The tree leans right-right (10 → 20 → 30), so one left rotation makes 20 the root.

questions.question: P1, P2 and P3 all arrive at time 0, in that order, with bursts 5, 3 and 1. With round robin and a time quantum of 2, the average turnaround time is:
questions.explanation: Gantt: P1 0–2, P2 2–4, P3 4–5, P1 5–7, P2 7–8, P1 8–9. Finish times 9, 8, 5: average 22/3.

questions.question: With 3 frames, how many page faults does the optimal (OPT) algorithm cause for the reference string 7 0 1 2 0 3 0 4 2 3 0 3 2 1 2 0 1 7 0 1?
questions.explanation: OPT replaces the page used farthest in the future; this classic string gives 9 (LRU 12, FIFO 15).

questions.question: Belady's anomaly, where adding frames can increase page faults, can occur with:
questions.explanation: LRU and OPT are stack algorithms and never show the anomaly.

questions.question: How many times is x printed?
questions.explanation: Parent's first fork makes C1 (which skips the rest and prints). The second fork makes C2 (prints). The parent, with both forks true, forks C3. Four processes print.

questions.question: The disk head is at cylinder 50. Requests: 82, 170, 43, 140, 24, 16, 190. With SSTF scheduling, the total head movement is:
With umask 027, a newly created directory gets the permissions:
questions.explanation: Directories start from 777: 777 − 027 = 750 (files start from 666 and get 640).

questions.question: What does setfacl -m u:ravi:rw report.txt do?
options: makes ravi the owner of report.txt
gives user ravi read and write access without changing the file's owner or group
adds ravi to the file's group
questions.explanation: An ACL entry adds per-user rights on top of the owner/group/other bits; getfacl shows it.

questions.question: What does awk -F: '$3 >= 1000 { print $1 }' /etc/passwd print?
options: the first 1000 lines of the file
the users whose home directory is longer than 1000 characters
the third field of every line
the usernames whose UID is 1000 or more
questions.explanation: -F: sets the field separator; field 3 is the UID and field 1 the username (regular users usually start at 1000).

questions.question:
In a folder with a.txt and b.txt, what does this loop do?
for f in *.txt; do mv "$f" "${f%.txt}.bak"; done
options: renames them to a.txt.bak and b.txt.bak
renames them to a.bak and b.bak
copies them to a.bak and b.bak, keeping the originals
questions.explanation: ${f%.txt} removes the shortest .txt suffix from the end of $f.

questions.explanation: Bash arrays start at index 0, and ${#a[@]} is the number of elements.

questions.question: On Ubuntu you change the mirror in /etc/apt/sources.list. What must you run before apt install picks it up?
questions.explanation: apt update downloads the package lists from the configured mirrors.

questions.question: Which statement about MBR and GPT is correct?
options: MBR supports up to 128 primary partitions
GPT disks cannot boot with UEFI
MBR disks can be up to 16 TiB with 512-byte sectors
GPT supports disks larger than 2 TiB and 128 partitions by default
questions.explanation: MBR: 4 primary partitions, 2 TiB limit with 512-byte sectors. GPT: 128 entries by default, used by UEFI.

questions.question: Which order creates a usable LVM logical volume on a new disk /dev/sdb?
questions.explanation: Physical volume → volume group → logical volume → file system.

questions.question: Which Windows command shows the IP address, subnet mask, gateway, DNS servers and MAC address of every adapter?
questions.explanation: ipconfig /all is the Windows counterpart of ip addr plus resolver details.

questions.question: From 192.168.10.0/24 you need equal subnets, each with at least 50 usable hosts. How many such subnets can you make?
questions.explanation: 50 hosts need 6 host bits (62 hosts): /26, and a /24 holds four /26 subnets.

questions.question: Which of these is a usable host address in 10.0.8.0/21?
The shortest valid form of the IPv6 address 2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:ff00:0042:8329 is:
questions.explanation: Drop leading zeros in each group and replace the longest run of zero groups with ::.

questions.question: Ignoring overheads, how long does it take to send a 10 MB file (10 × 10⁶ bytes) over an 8 Mbps link?
questions.explanation: 80 × 10⁶ bits / 8 × 10⁶ bit/s = 10 s.

questions.question: A signal travels 2000 km through a cable at 2 × 10⁸ m/s. The propagation delay is:
In stop-and-wait, a frame takes 1 ms to transmit and the one-way propagation delay is 4 ms. Ignoring ACK size and processing, the link utilisation is about:
Which pair of default ports is correct?
questions.explanation: IMAP 143 / IMAPS 993; POP3 110 / POP3S 995; 465 and 587 are SMTP submission.

questions.question: IEEE 802.11ac (Wi-Fi 5) operates in:
questions.explanation: 802.11ac is 5 GHz only; 802.11n and 802.11ax use both bands.

questions.question: On a Cisco switch, which command lists the VLANs and the access ports assigned to each?
questions.explanation: show vlan brief gives VLAN IDs, names, status and member ports; trunks are shown by show interfaces trunk.

questions.question: The prompt Router(config-if)# shows that you are in:
questions.explanation: Router> user EXEC, Router# privileged, (config)# global, (config-if)# interface, (config-line)# line.

questions.question: Which command lists the listening TCP ports together with the owning processes on a modern Linux system?
questions.explanation: -t TCP, -l listening, -n numeric, -p process; ss replaces netstat.

questions.question: Hosts in VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 on the same switch must talk to each other. What is required?
options: nothing; a switch forwards between VLANs by default
a hub between the two VLANs
a DNS server for each VLAN
a Layer-3 device: a router (e.g. router-on-a-stick) or a Layer-3 switch
questions.explanation: VLANs are separate broadcast domains; traffic between them must be routed.

questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN keeps every student: Asha matches 2 rows, Bilal 1, and Chen and Divya 1 each with NULL marks: 5.

questions.question: Using the table shown, what does the query return?
questions.explanation: The average is (30 + 50 + 70 + 90)/4 = 60; C (70) and D (90) are above it.

questions.question: Using the table shown, what does the query return?
questions.explanation: The inner query finds the top salary (90); the outer MAX below it is the second highest.

questions.question: R(A, B, C, D) has the dependencies AB → C, C → D and D → A. Its candidate keys are:
questions.explanation: B appears on no right side, so every key has B. AB, BC (C→D→A) and BD (D→A, AB→C) each determine everything.

questions.question: A schedule is conflict-serializable exactly when:
options: its precedence (conflict) graph has no cycle
transactions never read the same item
questions.explanation: An acyclic precedence graph gives a serial order by topological sort.

questions.question: In GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON college.* TO 'lab'@'%';, the % means that:
options: it gets privileges on all databases
the account may connect from any host
the grant expires after one session
questions.explanation: % is a wildcard in the host part; college.* limits it to the college database.

questions.question: mysqldump --single-transaction is mainly used to:
options: restore a backup in one transaction
take a consistent backup of InnoDB tables without locking them
back up only the last transaction log
questions.explanation: It starts a REPEATABLE READ transaction and dumps a consistent snapshot.

questions.question: A table has a composite index on (dept, sal). Which WHERE clause can use this index?
questions.explanation: A composite index works from its leftmost column; a function on the column also prevents index use.

questions.question: Which command lists all KVM/libvirt virtual machines, including those that are shut off?
questions.explanation: Plain virsh list shows only running domains.

questions.question: Postfix, commonly installed on Linux mail servers, is:
questions.explanation: Postfix moves mail with SMTP; Dovecot is the usual IMAP/POP3 server.

questions.question: To serve a site over HTTPS with Apache on Ubuntu, you need:
options: only to open port 443 in the firewall
to rename the site's files to .https
to set Listen 80 ssl in ports.conf
mod_ssl enabled and a virtual host on port 443 with SSLCertificateFile and SSLCertificateKeyFile
questions.explanation: a2enmod ssl, then a :443 virtual host pointing to the certificate and key (for example from Let's Encrypt).

questions.question: Which selector has the highest specificity?
questions.explanation: #main p = (1,0,1); .content p.note = (0,2,1); div.content p = (0,1,2); one id beats any number of classes.

questions.question: To show how the exam scores of 200 students are distributed across score ranges, which Matplotlib function fits best?
questions.explanation: A histogram groups values into bins and shows the count in each.

questions.question: In OpenStack, which service provides compute (it runs the virtual machines)?
questions.explanation: Nova = compute, Swift = object storage, Neutron = networking, Keystone = identity.

partc.title: Official letter (10 marks, about 150 words).
partc.prompt: As the Head of the CSE Department, write to the Registrar requesting sanction to renew the annual maintenance contract (AMC) for the department's eight lab servers, which expires on 31 December. The renewal costs Rs. 3.6 lakh. Two quotations are enclosed, and a copy should go to the Finance Officer.
partc.guide: Format 3: sender's office and address, letter number and date, "To, The Registrar, ...", subject line, reference if any, "Sir/Madam,", body, "Yours faithfully,", signature with name and designation, "Encl.: Two quotations" and "Copy to: The Finance Officer". Content 4: what (AMC renewal for 8 servers), why (expiry on 31 December, risk of unsupported downtime, academic work affected), cost (Rs. 3.6 lakh, lowest quotation recommended), the request (sanction before the expiry date). Language 3: formal, polite, active requests ("It is requested that..."), no contractions, about 150 words.

partc.title: Incident report (10 marks, about 200 words).
partc.prompt: On Monday at 10:15 am a lab PC was infected with ransomware from a student's USB drive. Files on the shared project drive were encrypted before the PC was isolated at 10:40 am. The drive was restored from the previous night's backup and service resumed at 4:30 pm; one morning's work was lost. Write an incident report.
partc.guide: Format 3: title, incident number, date and time of the incident and of the report, location, reported by, then headed sections: Summary, Timeline, Impact, Cause, Action taken, Preventive measures, signature with name and designation. Content 4: timeline (10:15 infection, 10:40 isolation, restore, 4:30 pm resumption: about 6 h 15 min of downtime), impact (shared project drive unavailable, one morning's work lost), cause (malware on a USB drive, autorun or user execution, missing endpoint protection or USB policy), actions (isolation, scan, restore from backup, password resets if needed), prevention (USB blocking or scanning, updated antivirus, user awareness, backup verification, least-privilege share permissions). Language 3: past tense, factual, no blame on the student by name, about 200 words.

partc_note: Self-marking out of 10 each: format 3, content 4, language 3.
